prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep my configuration. B023 is the only shortlisted candidate on which every member who commented accepts the merit and the credit: a general, ligand-controlled method that replaced harsh aryl amine chemistry, used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, mechanistically understood, and confirmed for more than 25 years, with Buchwald and Hartwig as the clear independent originators. Aqvist and Zou both agree that Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide work was not the general catalytic method, which settles the credit question for me. On the 2010 overlap, the prize covered C-C bond formation; C-N coupling required its own ligand generations and a different mechanistic problem (amine binding, deprotonation, reductive elimination from an amido complex), so I treat it as a new advance, not a repeat. B060 remains the one candidacy with broad cross-field presence: three members carry it into their configurations, three more list it as an alternative, and Liu is named as decisive originator in every statement that discusses it. Chabes's reply clarified what was chemically new, which was my own test: an evolved TadA acting on DNA, site-specific and free of double-strand breaks, is a designed chemical outcome. Taken together, the two parts are one classical bond-forming method and one chemical-biology capability, three names in all.
statement.case_against: The pairing is a pragmatic coalition, not a thematically unified prize, and Chabes and Brzezinski both note that the partner for B060 is not agreed. B060 is young, its clinical record is short, it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, and Liu alone leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida. B023 can be read as an extension of the 2010 prize. If the committee does not accept B060 as chemistry, the prize reduces to B023 alone, which is clean but conservative.

responses.point: Explained that base editing is chemically new because deamination was made site-specific, evolved to act on DNA (TadA was an RNA enzyme) and kept free of double-strand breaks, while conceding it is less of a bond-forming advance than Buchwald-Hartwig. Chabes pairs B060 with B041 (Crews and Deshaies).
responses.response: That answers my question about chemical novelty and I accept it; I have moved from asking whether B060 is chemistry to asking only whether it is mature enough. I do not follow you to B041 as the partner. Your own case against notes that omitting Ciulli, Handa and the cereblon strand leaves a visible credit gap, and no PROTAC is approved. A prize pairing two chemical-biology items also gives up the classical core. B023 is mature, cleanly credited, and fits the same three-name limit with Liu, so I think it is the better second part. We agree on Liu alone.

responses.point: Pairs B060 with Gray and Winkler (B030) as a mechanistic physical-chemistry result plus a chemical capability, but states he is the only member to rank B030 and does not oppose B023 as better supported.
responses.response: I respect the clarity of the electron-tunnelling work, but by your own account B030 has no other first-place or top-three support and you call it mature and arguably late with no single dated breakthrough. That is hard for me to carry into a five-vote majority. Your statement that you would not oppose B023 is the important point: Liu plus Buchwald and Hartwig uses the same three names as Liu plus Gray and Winkler, and it is the version where the second part has several supporters. I would ask you to consider moving to B023 as the second part.

responses.point: Supports B023 alone as the strongest combination of consequence, maturity and clean credit, would keep Kosugi out of the credited names, and wants the 2010 overlap addressed explicitly.
responses.response: We agree on the pair and on Kosugi. I have addressed the 2010 point above: C-N coupling needed different ligands and mechanism. I accept that B023 alone would be a defensible prize. Where we differ is whether to add a second part. B023 alone has only two explicit supporters, and your alternatives list B060, so I ask whether you would accept Liu as the second part to reach a majority rather than leaving it at two votes. I would also support recording Kosugi's precedent in the background document.

responses.point: Stands for B041 alone (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) as a molecular design principle that redefines druggability, with the cereblon glue strand as an acknowledged attribution gap.
responses.response: I find the design principle convincing, and the VHL ligand and ternary-complex work is real chemistry. My difficulty is still timing and credit: no approved degrader, and a split between PROTAC and glue strands that three names cannot cover without a visible omission. If approvals or a clearer allocation emerge I would revisit it, which is why it stays among my alternatives. I note that you list B060 as an alternative, so there may be room to work together on Liu.

responses.point: Is the sole supporter of B039 (Deamer, Akeson, Bayley) and in the chair's summary acknowledges that Branton and Kasianowicz are excluded by a three-person cut.
responses.response: The chair's summary lays out the credit problem fairly: any three-name cut omits Branton or Kasianowicz, and the committee has not agreed which. Separately, much of the decisive step is engineering of pores and motor proteins, and I ask what was new chemically. I keep B039 as an alternative, not a lead, and will not press it against your own concerns.

uncertainties: Whether five members will accept a two-part prize built from a classical method and a chemical-biology candidate, given the partners paired with B060 differ.
Whether B023's overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize is judged mild or disqualifying by colleagues; Zou has asked directly.
Whether B060 is judged mature and distinct enough from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether Kondo and Nishida should share credit.
Kosugi's priority rests on my recollection of the history, supported but not verified by colleagues' statements.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent: my profile lists no mentor, collaborator or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate. Pd-catalyzed coupling is close to my own field of synthetic methodology, which I disclose as a disciplinary bias, not a personal tie. I share a Lund affiliation with the chair Linke and with Sparr, but neither has a candidate that I credit.
